pharm: Blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors on smooth muscle, relaxing spasm of the gastrointestinal, biliary, and genitourinary tracts and the uterine cervix
quick: 8 mg IM/IV for spasm; obstetric cervical dilatation 8 mg IM/IV, repeatable (per regional product information)
Oral forms may be taken before meals; follow local product information
Used intrapartum for cervical dilatation under supervision; otherwise use only if clearly needed
Anticholinergics may reduce milk; use with caution
No specific interaction; additive sedation possible
Heart rate, anticholinergic effects, fetal/uterine status in obstetric use
summary: Valethamate bromide is a quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic antispasmodic used (mainly in India and parts of Asia) to relieve smooth-muscle spasm of the GI, biliary, and genitourinary tracts and to hasten cervical dilatation during labor. It is not FDA-approved; dosing and indications are based on regional product information.
indications: Smooth-muscle spasm of the gastrointestinal tract (e.g. spastic colitis, intestinal/biliary colic) - per regional product information
Renal and ureteric colic / genitourinary spasm
Acceleration of cervical dilatation during the first stage of labor (obstetric use, per regional product information)

dosage.d: 8 mg by IM or slow IV injection, or oral tablets per local product information
dosage.t: Repeat as required per regional guidance
dosage.n: Not FDA-defined; follow regional product information

dosage.r: Slow cervical dilatation in first-stage labor
dosage.d: 8 mg IM or IV, may be repeated at intervals (e.g. every 30 minutes) up to a stated maximum per local guidance
dosage.t: During first stage of labor under supervision
dosage.n: Administer only under obstetric supervision with fetal monitoring

admin: Give parenterally (IM or slow IV) for acute spasm, or orally as directed by the regional product information
For obstetric use, administer only under supervision with maternal and fetal monitoring
Have atropine-reversal and resuscitation measures available for anticholinergic effects
moa: Valethamate bromide is a quaternary ammonium antimuscarinic agent that competitively blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors on smooth muscle. This relaxes spasm of the gastrointestinal, biliary, and genitourinary smooth muscle and the uterine cervix, relieving colic and facilitating cervical dilatation during labor.

absolute: Prostatic hypertrophy / bladder neck obstruction with urinary retention
Paralytic ileus, pyloric or other GI obstruction
relative: Hyperthyroidism, coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure
monitor: Heart rate and anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, blurred vision, retention)
Fetal heart rate and uterine activity in obstetric use

preg: When used intrapartum to assist cervical dilatation, valethamate is given under obstetric supervision. Outside this use, safety in pregnancy is not well established and it should be used only if clearly needed. Follow the regional product information.
lact: Anticholinergic agents may suppress lactation and small amounts may enter breast milk. Use with caution during breastfeeding and follow local product information.
renal: Specific dose adjustments in renal impairment are not well defined; use with caution as anticholinergic effects (e.g. urinary retention) may be more pronounced.
hepatic: Specific dose adjustments in hepatic impairment are not well defined; use with caution.

moderate: Other anticholinergics (antihistamines, tricyclic antidepressants, antiparkinson agents) - additive antimuscarinic effects
Drugs whose GI absorption is affected by reduced motility (e.g. digoxin) may have altered absorption
minor: Antacids/adsorbents may reduce absorption of oral anticholinergics if taken together
interactions.food: Oral forms typically taken before meals per regional product information
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; additive CNS depression possible
interactions.diagnostics: Anticholinergic effects (tachycardia, mydriasis) may confound clinical assessment

serious: Acute urinary retention (especially with prostatic hypertrophy)
emergency: Anticholinergic toxidrome (hot/dry skin, dilated pupils, delirium, tachycardia)

monitoring: Anticholinergic adverse effects (dry mouth, vision, urinary retention)
In obstetric use: fetal heart rate, uterine contractions, and progress of labor
counsel: This medicine relaxes muscle cramps/spasms; you may notice dry mouth, blurred vision, or a faster heartbeat
Report difficulty passing urine, eye pain or vision changes, or a very fast heartbeat
Tell your clinician if you have glaucoma, prostate problems, or heart disease
Use caution driving until you know how it affects your vision
pk: Rapid antispasmodic effect after IM/IV injection
Effect within minutes after parenteral dosing (regional data)
Short duration; repeat dosing as required per regional guidance
Store as directed on the product packaging
pearls: Valethamate bromide is NOT FDA-approved; it is marketed mainly in India/Asia. Dosing and indications here reflect regional product information, not an FDA label
Quaternary ammonium structure limits CNS penetration but it carries the usual antimuscarinic contraindications (glaucoma, urinary retention, GI obstruction, myasthenia gravis)
A common regional use is to hasten cervical dilatation in first-stage labor - this must be done under obstetric supervision with fetal monitoring; evidence for benefit is mixed
Atropine-like overdose is treated supportively; physostigmine may reverse severe central anticholinergic effects
Verify dose against the specific local product label, as formulations vary
missed: For scheduled oral dosing, if a dose is missed take it as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it. Parenteral/obstetric dosing is given by a clinician as needed, not on a fixed self-administered schedule.
overdose: Overdose produces an anticholinergic toxidrome: dry mouth, flushing, dilated pupils, blurred vision, tachycardia, urinary retention, and in severe cases agitation, delirium, hyperthermia, and arrhythmias. Treatment is supportive with airway/cardiac monitoring; physostigmine may be used for severe central anticholinergic toxicity, and benzodiazepines for agitation/seizures. Contact a poison control center.
